headline: Kansas Rancher Proves Wind and Cattle Can Thrive Together
meta_description: A Kansas cattle rancher has operated 50 wind turbines across his 7,000-acre ranch for two decades while his herd grazes peacefully below.
summary_short: For 20 years, a Kansas rancher has successfully run 50 wind turbines on his 7,000-acre cattle ranch, with wind royalties now covering roughly half his annual income.
body:
A Kansas rancher has operated 50 wind turbines across his 7,000-acre cattle ranch for two decades, proving that renewable energy and livestock farming can coexist without conflict.

The turbines have become more than an environmental asset—they've transformed the rancher's finances. Wind royalties now provide roughly half his annual income, a significant contribution that demonstrates how farmers can diversify revenue streams while supporting clean energy development.

The cattle continue to graze beneath the towering turbines as they have for the past 20 years, undisturbed by the rotating blades above them. This long-term success story challenges the notion that wind farms and traditional ranching are incompatible, offering a practical model for rural landowners seeking sustainable economic alternatives.
quick_facts: 50 wind turbines operating on 7,000-acre Kansas ranch
Two decades of successful coexistence with cattle
Wind royalties comprise roughly half of rancher's income
